name: Clock
description: A large clock with the date; 12/24-hour and seconds are set per copy
author: Lattice

sections.title: Reading it
items: The big line is the time; the line under it is the date as month, day and weekday.
Seconds are off by default — a clock that changes every second keeps pulling your eye back to it.
It only ticks while the card is visible. A hidden card costs nothing, and the time is right again the moment you look.

sections.title: 12-hour, 24-hour, seconds
items: Click the clock on the desktop, then use the inspector on the right.
12-hour clock off means 24-hour, e.g. 21:40. On gives 9:40 PM.
Show seconds adds them and widens the digits so the card does not jitter.

sections.title: Each copy keeps its own settings
items: Two clocks on one desktop can show different formats — settings belong to the copy, not to the widget.
Changes apply immediately; the card is redrawn, not reloaded.

sections.title: If it shows --:--
items: The platform did not allow reading the time. The widget asks for it, so it needs the clock permission.
Grant it again and the card recovers on its next tick — no restart needed.

changes: 12-hour clock and Show seconds moved into the inspector, so each copy can differ.
Ticks on the platform scheduler: a hidden clock stops working instead of burning power.
No longer needs the storage permission — settings live with the platform, not inside the widget.
First release: large time, date and weekday line.
